workflow: Collecting, organizing, and prioritizing user feedback from multiple channels (email, support tickets, social media, in-app) into a single product roadmap.
trigger: Inability to track and act on user feedback scattered across disparate tools.
current_workaround: Manually exporting feedback from various sources into a spreadsheet or a single document, then manually categorizing and prioritizing it.
consequence: Missed or delayed product improvements, frustrated users, and wasted engineering time on low-impact features.

workflow: Manually tagging, categorizing, and routing support tickets to the appropriate team member or department.
trigger: High volume of incoming support requests that need to be sorted and assigned.
current_workaround: Using a shared email inbox or a basic ticketing system and manually reading each ticket to determine its category and assignee.
consequence: Slow response times, misrouted tickets, and increased agent burnout.

workflow: Repurposing long-form content (blog posts, webinars, podcasts) into multiple short-form social media posts, emails, and other assets.
trigger: Need to maintain a consistent content marketing cadence across multiple channels.
current_workaround: Manually re-reading or re-watching content, extracting key quotes and ideas, and rewriting them for each platform.
consequence: Inconsistent brand messaging, missed content distribution opportunities, and significant time investment.

workflow: Researching and personalizing outbound sales emails by manually looking up prospects on LinkedIn, company websites, and other sources.
trigger: Need to generate qualified leads and book meetings.
current_workaround: Switching between multiple browser tabs and tools to gather information about a prospect before writing a personalized email.
consequence: Low email response rates, inefficient use of SDR time, and reduced pipeline generation.

workflow: Creating and distributing recurring reports by manually querying databases, exporting data to spreadsheets, and building charts and dashboards.
trigger: Weekly or monthly business review meetings requiring updated metrics.
current_workaround: Writing SQL queries, copying results into Excel or Google Sheets, and manually formatting charts and tables for presentation.
consequence: Delayed insights, data inconsistencies, and analysts spending more time on reporting than on analysis.

workflow: Managing and tracking software development tasks, bugs, and feature requests across multiple projects and teams.
trigger: Lack of visibility into what different teams are working on and the status of various tasks.
current_workaround: Using a combination of spreadsheets, sticky notes, and multiple project management tools that don't integrate well.
consequence: Missed deadlines, duplicated work, and difficulty in prioritizing tasks.

workflow: Screening and shortlisting job applicants by manually reviewing resumes and cover letters.
trigger: Receiving a high volume of applications for an open position.
current_workaround: Reading through each resume and cover letter to identify candidates that match the job requirements.
consequence: Slow hiring process, potential to overlook qualified candidates, and recruiter fatigue.

workflow: Monitoring customer health scores and identifying at-risk accounts by manually checking usage data, support tickets, and NPS scores.
trigger: Proactive need to prevent churn and ensure customer satisfaction.
current_workaround: Logging into multiple tools (product analytics, support platform, CRM) to gather data and manually calculating a health score.
consequence: Missed churn signals, reactive rather than proactive customer management, and lost revenue.

workflow: Scheduling and publishing social media posts across multiple platforms (LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Facebook) at optimal times.
trigger: Need to maintain a consistent social media presence without being online 24/7.
current_workaround: Manually logging into each social media platform to post content, or using a basic scheduling tool that lacks advanced features.
consequence: Inconsistent posting schedule, missed engagement opportunities, and time wasted on repetitive tasks.

workflow: Reconciling invoices and payments by manually matching bank statements against accounting records.
trigger: End-of-month or end-of-quarter financial close process.
current_workaround: Downloading bank statements, exporting invoices from accounting software, and manually comparing line items in a spreadsheet.
consequence: Errors in financial reporting, delayed close, and increased audit risk.
